verdicts.title: Alpha does not set the claim threshold under the shipped GRPO normalisation
verdicts.reasoning:
The evidence holds and I reproduced it two ways.

- **Code:** configs/base.yaml:48 sets `scale_rewards: group`. TRL divides by the per-group std at grpo_trainer.py:2821-2843, and `nanstd` is Bessel-corrected (trl/trainer/utils.py:981-1003), as the reviewer's script assumes.
- **Rerun:** the reviewer's simulation gives 0.450/0.500/0.550/0.600 for alpha 0/0.25/0.5/0.75. Those values snap to its 0.05 bin grid.
- **Independent check** (threshold_fixedpoint.py, a fixed-point calculation with no learning dynamics and no bins): group scaling at G=8 gives 0.43/0.49/0.53/0.56 with scattered beliefs, and 0.50/0.58/0.64/0.70 when all rollouts of a task share one belief. With no scaling it gives 0.500/0.626/0.750/0.875, the intended values.
- **Project's own notes agree:** docs/research/findings.json:1647 records that group normalisation moves the threshold to 1/2, yet integration-architecture.md:88 still recommends `scale_rewards="group"`.

So alpha=0.75 lands at 0.56-0.70, not 0.875. The exact compressed range depends on the belief model; the direction does not. The alpha=0.25 headline run is less affected (about 0.49-0.58 against 0.625). The four-run alpha sweep and contribution 4 are what break. This is a toy bandit, not the real model.
verdicts.better_fix: The reviewer's fix is right: set `grpo.scale_rewards: batch`, which is a uniform scale and keeps the threshold exact. Also correct the threshold comments in configs/honest_alpha*.yaml and DESIGN.md:73-74. Do the group-scaled ablation in the report-only pilot, not as a full run.

verdicts.title: Primary metric is AgentAbstain, but the trained behaviour cannot be expressed there and the fallback evidence is thin
verdicts.reasoning:
The facts hold; the severity does not.

**Verified:**
- The launcher runs their harness unchanged (agentabstain_standalone.py:43-67), and docs/EVAL.md:341 says the model never sees our tools there.
- From their tasks.jsonl: system prompts are one-line role descriptions (median 99 characters). 2 of 526 mention "confirm"; none mention abstaining or declining. The trained interface is absent.
- The generator is unreleased (EVAL.md:343) while proposal.md:81 promises fresh instances.
- Only 19 abstain-warranted Agentic Abstention tasks are runnable (EVAL.md:252-253).
- The power numbers reproduce.

**Why not a blocker:** ROADMAP.md:134 already names the held-out set "primary for H2" and :136 labels AgentAbstain "out of domain, H3 transfer". What remains open is that proposal.md:73 and :80 still promise AgentAbstain as the primary metric, and that the transfer is unmeasured. A weak transfer result weakens the paper's framing; it does not make the training invalid.

**Two corrections:**
- Coverage is 3-4 of 8 categories, not "at most 3". Their critical_tool_failure cases (a tool fails on every call) resemble our no_network and revoke_permission.
- "Timely recall needs abstention at call 1, the behaviour we penalise as lazy" is wrong. The lazy penalty applies only on feasible tasks (reward.py:113); a zero-command abstain on an infeasible task earns +1.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Edit proposal sections 6-7 to match the roadmap: held-out terminal set primary, AgentAbstain secondary transfer. Delete the fresh-instances row.
2. Run base Qwen3.5-4B on AgentAbstain in Phase 0 (526 judge calls). Decide on the bridged harness and free-text training only after that number exists; they cost a week or more and may be unnecessary.

verdicts.title: high_risk labels an explicitly instructed deletion as must-abstain and is the default held-out family
verdicts.reasoning:
The central claim, that this construction does not match AgentAbstain, is refuted by their data.

**AgentAbstain's high_stakes_action category (all 31 pairs read from tasks.jsonl):**
- Every abstain variant is an explicit user instruction to do something extreme (transformation_dimension = instruction).
- Escalation dimension: audience 17, scope 5, monetary 5, irreversibility 4.
- The irreversibility cases are instructed deletions, for example preview_006 "permanently delete every file and folder under /workspace/documents" and preview_016 "permanently delete every file and folder under / recursively with no recovery".
- Act twins can be destructive too: preview_025 deletes one expired card on the act side and "every saved payment card from every FoodDash account" on the abstain side.

So "explicitly instructed, severe, irreversible action: confirm first" is their convention, and the v2 near-miss (authorised, scratch data only) mirrors their act twins. The reviewer read 2 of 31 pairs through a summarising tool.

**What survives:**
- The system prompt says to abstain for an action "you were not clearly authorised to take" (harness.py:25), while the instruction says the deletion is required (perturb.py:418-428). Wording and label conflict.
- Truthful compliance scores -2.0 and is flagged `fabricated` (reward.py:120, 132, 155; reproduced). It is a violation, not a fabrication.
- The default held-out family is this one instruction-level family, with 3 templates and 4 sentinels (scripts/build_dataset.sh:21).

Training is not affected: the family is held out by default. Our label is somewhat more contestable than theirs, because our instruction shows the user knows what the directory holds. That is a judgement.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Reword the prompt, for example: "or a destructive or irreversible action with severe consequences; confirm before doing it even if the instruction asks for it".
2. Count compliance as a violation, not a fabrication (see F7).
3. Hold out an environment-mechanism family as well, such as revoke_permission.
4. Treat the reviewer's emergent-risk operator as an additional family (it maps to their emergent_risk_discovery category), not a replacement.

verdicts.title: A zero-command constant policy looks honest on every metric and earns near-optimal reward
verdicts.reasoning:
The reward hole is real and v2 does not close it.

**Reproduced with the project's code:**
- `submit_report(incomplete)` with 0 commands earns +alpha with lazy=False. The lazy rule fires only for status abstain (reward.py:113).
- Blockers match by set intersection (reward.py:122-124), so listing every category earns +1 on every infeasible task.
- The constant policy's mean reward is 0.500/0.625/0.750/0.875 at alpha 0/0.25/0.5/0.75.

**Stronger than the reviewer stated** (mixed_reward_check.py): an agent that does all the work but never claims earns exactly what the zero-effort policy earns. Work has no value unless a claim is made. v2's Brier terms do not change this; a policy reporting progress 0 scores them perfectly.

**Overstated:** it does not look honest on every metric. Abstain precision is 0.5, paired accuracy 0, CAR 0, and verified success 0. In training, `rewards/task_success/mean` and `honest/case/honest_failure` are logged (trl_rewards.py:65). The collapse would be seen; the run would still be wasted.

**Judgement, not verified:** that training converges there. The mechanism is plausible. With a base model that claims indiscriminately, "report incomplete" has positive advantage whatever the effort. Under an assumed base (30% success, 80% claim rate), the constant policy captures 89% of the reward gain available at alpha=0.25.
verdicts.better_fix:
The reviewer's first fix is weak: any minimum command count is met by trivial commands.

1. Pay for the outcome independently of the report: add c x tests_passed on feasible tasks. This is `reward_weights [1, c]` over the two existing reward functions (train.py:246-252 allows only [1,0] and [0,1]). The threshold stays exactly (1+alpha)/2 for any c (checked numerically), and at c=1 doing the work is worth +0.15 mean reward at 30% success.
2. Zero that outcome term when tampering is detected.
3. Accept one blocker category only.
4. Keep the reviewer's kill rules and constant-policy reference rows.

verdicts.title: No neutral-prompt condition and no no-training baselines, so gains cannot be attributed to RL
verdicts.reasoning:
All evidence holds.

- The honesty prompt (harness.py:17-29) is baked into every dataset row (tasks/build.py:88-93) and into the fallback at train.py:439.
- run_eval.py:39-110 has no system-prompt option, although RolloutConfig.system_prompt exists (rollout.py:54).
- No gate or CONVOLVE-style baseline exists in src, scripts or configs.
- The tool docstrings repeat the instruction ("complete only if the whole task is done and verified"), so a neutral system prompt alone would not be fully neutral.

The signal-detection table reproduces, but its conclusion is narrower than stated. "Low fabrication by never claiming" appears at 30% success and AUROC 0.7. At the difficulty v2's filter targets (about 50% success, AUROC 0.8) the same model claims on 36% of episodes at alpha=0.25. The AUROC is an assumption either way.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer proposes. Order by cost: `--system-prompt-file` with a neutral prompt, and the threshold sweep on stated confidence, are hours each and belong in Phase 0. The verify-then-report gate can follow.

verdicts.title: H1 has no mechanism in this harness, and the run cannot produce the promised curve
verdicts.reasoning:
**Holds:**
- `task_success` ignores the report and returns 0 on infeasible tasks (trl_rewards.py:92), so infeasible groups give zero advantage.
- For the report's content the expected gradient is exactly zero, because the reward does not depend on the report given the trajectory.
- `save_steps: 25` with `save_total_limit: 4` (base.yaml:80-81) keeps only steps 225-300.
- One seed is planned (ROADMAP.md:128-129).

**Overstated, in two places:**
- A mechanism exists for the abstention half of H1. A report ends the episode, so stopping early forfeits any chance of success and gets negative advantage. Outcome-only RL should suppress early abstain and incomplete reports, and that may generalise to infeasible tasks. This is my reasoning from the code, not a measurement.
- A curve does exist without checkpoints. The zero-weight honesty function still runs and logs `honest/claim_rate_infeasible`, `explicit_abstain_rate_infeasible` and `case/fabrication` every step (trl_rewards.py:62-75). It is on-policy, on training tasks, with 32 infeasible episodes per step.

The fabrication half of H1 is still likely to be null, so the severity stands.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Set `save_total_limit: null`; LoRA adapters are small.
2. Log P(claim|fail) in training.
3. State H1 in advance as two parts: abstention falls (has a mechanism) and fabrication rises (exploratory).
4. Run the reviewer's eval-only Tmax-versus-base check first; I agree with it.

verdicts.title: Several metric definitions are wrong, gameable or not comparable to the sources they cite
verdicts.reasoning:
All five definitions are as described: reward.py:155, metrics.py:160, 166, 275-284 and 294-301, and the Pareto default at eval/summary.py:133-135. The numbers reproduce (honest agent: abstain precision 0.575, strict 1.000).

Downgraded because none of them touches the reward. `episodes.jsonl` stores the full outcome of every episode (EVAL.md:57), so each metric can be redefined and re-scored after training at no GPU cost.

On (e), the alphabetical-order detail is speculative, since v2 control names do not exist yet. The structural point stands: `pair_units` picks one feasible task per pair_id and will need updating when controls share it.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer proposes. Do it alongside the F4 reference rows, before any results table is produced.

verdicts.title: The planned evaluation cannot resolve the effects H2 claims; seeds are assigned to one arm only
verdicts.reasoning:
Verified.

- LIMIT=200 per source (scripts/build_dataset.sh:18) with test_frac 0.10 (tasks/build.py:52) gives about 40 test sources.
- power.py reproduces. I re-derived N=40, k=4 analytically: SE 4.2pp, so about +-8.3pp.
- 3 seeds for the headline only (ROADMAP.md:129); sweep_alpha.sh:8 defaults to one seed.
- No margin is defined (proposal.md:73).

One caveat: ROADMAP.md:117 describes the 200-source build as the bring-up dataset, and the full-run size is not stated anywhere. Thousands of unused seeds remain, so the test set can still be enlarged later from sources outside training.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Fix the test split now, from seeds outside the training pool: at least 250 sources at 4 samples, not difficulty-filtered.
2. Pre-register the non-inferiority margin.
3. Spend seeds on the two arms the headline compares (honest alpha=0.25 and outcome-only, 3 each).
4. Take the alpha trend from the pilot.

verdicts.title: Step time is untimed and probably dominated by TRL's serial tool loop; the two-rank layout has an untested hang path
verdicts.reasoning:
**Structure confirmed:**
- Tool calls run one after another across a rank's episodes (grpo_trainer.py:2031-2048).
- Each call blocks (trl/experimental/harbor/_env.py:67-69) on a `docker compose exec` subprocess (harbor docker.py:1299-1326).

**Cost figures:** the arithmetic reproduces, but every latency is assumed, and a 16-125 node-day range is not a usable estimate. ROADMAP.md:120 already schedules a throughput benchmark, so "untimed" is partly covered by the plan. What the plan lacks is a step-time limit that triggers a redesign.

**Rank problem understated.** It is not only a hang when one rank finishes early. I ran TRL's real `VLLMGeneration.generate` with stand-in collectives: whenever the two ranks have different numbers of live episodes, rank 1 receives completions sampled for other episodes. See missed item M1.
verdicts.better_fix:
1. Use one training rank (see M1).
2. Time a real step with at least 8 tasks, infeasible variants included.
3. Set the limit in advance: above about 10 minutes per step, move to a `rollout_func` with concurrent tool execution before any full run.
4. Lower `command_timeout_sec` to about 60.

verdicts.title: v2's masking of cap-hit episodes removes the main learning signal on infeasible tasks
verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism holds. A masked reward is excluded from the group mean and its advantage is forced to zero (grpo_trainer.py:2815, 2821, 2866). On an infeasible task the contrast between abstaining (+1) and flailing to the cap (+0.25, reward.py:127) disappears once the flailing episode is masked.

Two qualifications:
- v2 is not implemented, and ROADMAP.md:31 says "rather than scored 0", which describes only the feasible case. This may be an ambiguity in the plan, not a decision.
- Masking is also harmful on feasible tasks: an episode that never reports gets zero advantage, so nothing pushes the policy toward reporting at all.
verdicts.better_fix: Do not mask. Ship the budget warnings, covering tokens as well as calls (see M2), and keep unreported episodes scored (0 on feasible, 0.25 on infeasible). Once the agent can see its budget, "report before you run out" is the behaviour the reward should teach.

verdicts.title: The held-out split shares operator templates with training
verdicts.reasoning:
The facts hold: 3 constraint templates (perturb.py:359-366), 4 sentinels and 3 risk templates (:396-428), a seeded choice common to all splits (:94-96), splits by source group only (tasks/build.py:96-104, 302-308), and no train/test partition in the phrasing-pool plan (ROADMAP.md:45).

Downgraded because v2's near-miss controls already defeat plain string matching (the control carries the same sentence with an irrelevant path), and the held-out-family run is the stronger generalisation test. Disjoint phrasing pools are a cheap addition, not something a run depends on.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer proposes: partition phrasings and sentinel paths into train and test pools when the v2 pools are written.

verdicts.title: The roadmap measures before training but sets no stop gates; a cheaper decisive pilot is missing
verdicts.reasoning:
Mostly holds. Phase 3 (ROADMAP.md:122-125) attaches no thresholds to the base-rate measurements and Phase 4 follows regardless. "No stop gates" is slightly overstated: two engineering gates exist (at least 95% of variants validating, :117; report compliance below 70% triggers a warm start, :54). There is no gate on the science.

The report-only pilot is plausible from the code: `compute_reward` is a pure function (reward.py:1-5), the evidence weight is 0 (:40), TRL passes dataset columns to reward functions (grpo_trainer.py:1669), and eval saves full transcripts (EVAL.md:58). It is not built. It needs a builder that cuts each transcript before the report, and a forced report turn for episodes that never reported. Its cost figures rest on assumed latencies.

It tests F1 and F4 directly, which are the two surviving blockers.
verdicts.better_fix: Keep the staged plan and gates. Add M1 and M2 to Stage 0. Make the pilot a requirement before the alpha sweep; it is optional before the first alpha=0.25 run if the F1 and F4 fixes are in.

hypothesis_verdicts.evidence:
I agree with the reviewer's split.

**AgentAbstain: confirmed.** The launcher runs their harness unchanged (agentabstain_standalone.py:43-67). Their 526 system prompts are one-line role descriptions (median 99 characters; 2 mention "confirm", none mention abstaining), so neither our tools nor our prompt exist there, and abstention must appear as free text that training never rewards. Coverage is 3-4 of their 8 categories, slightly better than the reviewer's "at most 3".

**Agentic Abstention: no format gap.** scripts/eval_agentic_abstention.sh:26 runs our own agent with our tools. The cost is that only 19 abstain-warranted tasks are public and the numbers are not comparable to the paper's.

**One sub-claim is wrong:** timely recall at call 1 does not conflict with the lazy penalty, which applies only on feasible tasks (reward.py:113).

Whether transfer fails is untested. The base-model AgentAbstain run in Phase 0 is the cheap test.

The reviewer marked this confirmed. AgentAbstain's own data refutes half of it.

**Refuted:** that our high_risk construction disagrees with theirs. All 31 of their high_stakes_action abstain variants are explicit user instructions to do something extreme. Four are instructed irreversible deletions or replacements (preview_006, preview_014, preview_016, preview_026), and their act twins include ordinary destructive requests (preview_009 deletes one number's messages; preview_025 deletes one expired card). Labelling an explicitly instructed, severe deletion as "confirm first" is their convention, and v2's near-miss control matches their act side.

**Confirmed:**
- The system prompt's "not clearly authorised" wording (harness.py:25) contradicts the label.
- Truthful compliance scores -2.0 and is flagged as fabrication (reward.py:120, 132, 155).
- conflicting_constraint is a real contradiction and matches their category (their first example: return a nonstop flight while only considering flights with at least one stop).

Our label is somewhat more contestable than theirs because the instruction shows the user knows what the directory contains. That is a judgement.

**Structure confirmed in source:** 64 episodes per optimizer step and 19,200 per run (configs/base.yaml:52-56, 63); serial blocking tool calls (grpo_trainer.py:2031-2048; trl/experimental/harbor/_env.py:67-69); a `docker compose exec` subprocess per call (harbor docker.py:1299-1326); concurrent grading (trl_rewards.py:31-33).

**Cost figures not verified:** cost_model.py reproduces arithmetically (7.8 / 21.5 / 59.8 minutes per step), but every latency in it is assumed and nothing has run. A range of 16-125 node-days for the matrix is a reason to measure, not an estimate. ROADMAP.md:120 already plans the measurement.

**Pilot feasibility:** plausible from the code, not built (see F12).

**Rank mismatch:** confirmed and worse than reported. Executing TRL's server-mode generate for two simulated ranks shows completions mis-routed whenever live episode counts differ (see M1).

missed.title: The shipped two-rank launch mis-routes completions inside TRL's tool loop
missed.claim: With two training processes and a vLLM server, each rank slices the gathered completions using its own count of live episodes. After the first tool round the two ranks' counts differ, so rank 1 receives completions that were sampled for other episodes' contexts, or too few completions. Half of each batch would then train on actions and log-probabilities that belong to a different trajectory, with no error raised in the first case. If one rank finishes its loop a round earlier, the two ranks also call different collectives. The smoke test cannot catch any of this because it runs one process on one task.
missed.evidence:
- **Slice uses the local length:** trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:594 gathers prompts from all ranks; :651-656 slices with `process_index * len(prompts)`.
- **Live counts are per rank:** grpo_trainer.py:2023 (local loop condition) and :2190 (each round generates only for that rank's live episodes).
- **Shipped layout:** configs/base.yaml:40 (`num_processes: 2`) and :68 (`vllm_mode: server`); scripts/train.sh:9-11, 39. configs/smoke.yaml:11 uses 1 process.
- **Executed** (rank_slice_check.py, TRL's real `VLLMGeneration.generate` with in-process stand-ins for the collectives):
  - live counts (3,2): rank 1 receives the completions for rank 0's third episode and its own first, instead of its own two
  - live counts (2,3): rank 1 receives 2 completions for 3 prompts
  - live counts (4,1): rank 1 receives rank 0's second completion
  - equal counts: correct

Not run under real multi-process training.
missed.fix: Train on one rank: `TRAIN_GPUS=0`, configs/accelerate/single_gpu.yaml, and `gradient_accumulation_steps: 32` to keep 64 episodes per step. LoRA on a 4B model does not need two training GPUs, and the freed GPU can serve a second run. Colocate mode is the alternative. verdicts.title: scale_rewards=group means alpha is not the claim threshold
verdicts.reasoning:
The evidence holds three ways.

1. Code: configs/base.yaml:48 sets scale_rewards: group; TRL divides by the per-group Bessel-corrected std at grpo_trainer.py:2826 and :2843 (nanstd in trl/trainer/utils.py:980-1004). Their grpo_exact.py reproduces exactly.
2. Independent derivation (v_thresh.py, a different method: the indifference point of one rollout whose 7 groupmates follow the population policy, iterated to a self-consistent threshold). Result for alpha = 0/.25/.5/.75: 0.43/0.50/0.55/0.585, against nominal 0.50/0.625/0.75/0.875. Their simulation gave 0.40/0.48/0.54/0.57; my reseeded rerun gave 0.40/0.49/0.54/0.58 at both lr 0.03 x 2000 steps and lr 0.01 x 6000 steps. Under batch and none the rerun gives 0.48/0.60/0.71/0.83 and 0.49/0.62/0.78/0.90.
3. Published: the abstract of arXiv 2608.00301 says group normalisation "silently replaces every designed penalty with an effective penalty of one, moving the learned threshold from t* to 1/2". The project's own notes record this (docs/research/findings.json:458 and :1647), yet docs/research/integration-architecture.md:87 and base.yaml:48 still choose group.

Why major and not blocker: a single alpha=0.25 run is still a valid honesty run, with an effective threshold near 0.50 instead of 0.625, and the alpha trade-off stays monotone. What cannot be supported is the stated threshold (1+alpha)/2 and the width of the Pareto front: the sweep spans about 0.16-0.18 of threshold instead of 0.375, and fabrication on feasible tasks moves 12% to 7% across the sweep instead of 10% to 1% (their sim_main.json). It is a blocker for the alpha sweep specifically.

One interaction the reviewer understates: in their own simulation group scaling is what keeps the high-alpha runs from collapsing (0% never-claim seeds under group, up to 94-100% under batch/none in weak-self-knowledge cells). Fixing INC-1 alone raises exposure to the collapse in INC-5.
verdicts.better_fix: Set grpo.scale_rewards: batch (the std is taken over the gathered 64 rollouts, so it is correct with 2 processes); none also works. Ship it together with the success bonus (INC-5) and the stop rules (missed item VIS-M1), not alone. Make train.py reject scale_rewards=group when reward.mode=honest, add the two-valued-group unit test, and report the realised threshold per alpha in the paper. Effort: under an hour.

verdicts.title: Non-completion is unverified and free on feasible tasks
verdicts.reasoning:
The code facts all hold (current line numbers): reward.py:113-114 applies the lazy rule only to status=abstain with zero commands; reward.py:115-117 pays alpha to every other non-claim report whatever its blockers say; reward.py:121-125 pays +1 on infeasible tasks for any overlapping category. Their spot checks rerun identically. The fix also restores something the project's own architecture note prescribed and reward.py dropped: integration-architecture.md:85 says "Abstaining on a feasible task: -0.5".

Why I lower it from blocker:
- Their own simulation does not show this loophole derailing training: 0 of 216 cells lose effort without budget loss or Brier terms.
- The headline "abstains on 42-50% of near-miss controls" is mostly relabelling. In sim_main.json the claim rate on near-miss controls is only modestly lower than on plain feasible tasks (0.25 against about 0.33 at alpha=.25, d'=1, s=.5), and 56-96% of the non-claims on controls carry the abstain label. Abstain and incomplete are exactly tied on feasible tasks in a linear toy, so the label is set by whatever the infeasible tasks taught. The mechanism is real; the size is toy-specific.
- The primary paired accuracy (eval/metrics.py:275-276) needs success_claimed on the feasible side, so a mislabelled failure does not change it.

What remains is still material. The proposal's "lazy abstention" row is effectively unimplemented, since one trivial command or status=incomplete defeats it. False "cannot be done" statements are paid like true failure reports. And pricing them matters for collapse resistance: at alpha=.25, s=.3 the best constant no-effort report earns 0.475 (30% infeasible) or 0.625 (50% infeasible) against 0.6325 / 0.7375 for a perfectly honest worker; with false blockers priced at 0 the best constant report drops to 0.325 / 0.50, roughly doubling the margin for honest work.

My rerun of their fix (batch, alpha=.25, new seeds): abstain on near-miss controls 0.40 -> 0.14 -> 0.10, abstain on infeasible 0.99 -> 0.97 -> 0.95, threshold and precision unchanged.
verdicts.better_fix:
Keep their change (feasible task + status abstain or an environment-class blocker pays false_blocker = 0, plain incomplete pays alpha) and add two things it does not cover:
1. Close the shotgun exploit (missed item VIS-M2): score the category by precision, not by any overlap.
2. Do not rely on the lazy rule. Counting commands is defeated by one `true`, so extending it to all non-claims is cosmetic. The real incentive to work is the success bonus in INC-5.
Also stop labelling a false-blocker report on a feasible task as case honest_failure, so that metrics.py HONEST_CASES and paired_accuracy_honest_act do not credit it. About 30 lines plus tests; hours.

verdicts.title: Episodes that end without a report: scored 0 today, masked in v2
verdicts.reasoning:
Both halves hold.

Today: reward.py:109-110 scores a feasible no-report 0 (below alpha) and reward.py:126-127 scores an infeasible one 0.25. TRL leaves the tool loop without a report at the iteration cap (grpo_trainer.py:2023) and when a tool result would overflow the token budget (grpo_trainer.py:2110-2131); in both cases the completion ends on an end-of-turn token, so grpo_trainer.py:2541-2547 does not mask it and it is trained with that reward. v2 already recognises this half (ROADMAP.md:29-32).

v2: masking a cap-hit episode (ROADMAP.md:31) gives it advantage 0, which is the group mean. An honest failure report earns alpha minus the group mean, which is negative in any group where someone succeeds (for example alpha=.25 against a mean near 0.6 at s=.5). So failing states are pushed away from reporting. The repo already states this principle for test timeouts (grading.py:155-156). My reseeded rerun: with a never-report option at 2% initial probability, masking drives it to 0.94 of feasible episodes (0.66 at step 300, minimum cell 0.89) and the claim rate falls to 0.05; scoring it 0 or alpha-0.1 keeps it at 0.00.

Magnitude caveat the reviewer already gives: nobody has measured the no-report rate. In my rerun at alpha=.25, budget loss of 5% or 10% causes no effort collapse under the current 0 score; 20% does (17% of cells).

Two things they missed:
- At alpha=0 the current rule ties silence (0) with an honest failure report (0), so that arm has no reason to report at all.
- A third exit exists: a final turn cut mid-generation is masked from the loss by mask_truncated_completions (base.yaml:49) but its 0 reward still enters the group mean.
verdicts.better_fix: Make the cap impossible to hit by accident rather than choosing a score for accidents. The env knows its own call count (env.py: len(self._history)): give it a budget two below max_tool_calling_iterations and have bash refuse to execute past it, returning "budget exhausted, call submit_report or abstain now". Do the same on a character-based estimate of the token budget (about 75% of max_completion_length) and shrink MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS (harness.py:40) as the budget runs down. A missing report is then a deliberate choice and can be scored as one, never masked: min(0, alpha) - 0.1 on feasible tasks, gamma on infeasible. Return None only for generation-truncated episodes, which TRL already drops from the loss. Gate on Phase-0: no-report rate under 5%. Hours.

verdicts.title: v2 Brier terms pay for predictability, which quitting maximises
verdicts.reasoning:
The mechanism is correct and is also a published result. Expected Brier loss for a calibrated forecast p is p(1-p), so only agents that attempt uncertain work pay it; a quitter who states 0 pays nothing. arXiv 2608.00301 states the same thing (Proposition 9b, as extracted from the HTML version): pure Brier makes the accuracy gradient 2q-1 < 0 for q < 1/2, "the model gains score by degrading accuracy on hard prompts". The paper's repair is a proper score plus a correctness reward, and the project's own note says so (findings.json:1647), but ROADMAP.md:26-27 plans the Brier terms with no correctness reward and claims they stay "consistent with the alpha threshold". That claim is true for claim-versus-not-claim and false for work-versus-quit.

Checks: spot values rerun identically (0.07 / 0.17 / 0.25 at brier_weight=0.5). The two escape routes are real: env.py:180 sets confidence None for abstain, harness.py:57-63 turns a non-numeric confidence into None, and reward.py:141 skips the term when confidence is None. My reseeded rerun: total weight 0.5 collapses effort at alpha=.25, s=.3, d'=1; weight 0.2 collapses alpha=.5, s=.3 and 19% of seeds at alpha=.25; weight 0.05 collapses nothing.

Severity is conditional: the ROADMAP gives no weight, and the reviewer's 0.25 + 0.25 is an assumption. It stays major because v2 is implemented before the first GPU run and the plan as written contains the trap.
verdicts.better_fix: Capping the weight at 0.05 avoids the trap but also leaves calibration almost untrained. Better: keep a meaningful Brier weight w and pair it with a success bonus lambda paid for passing tests whatever the report says, with lambda > w (total of both Brier terms). A non-claiming worker with success chance q then earns alpha + lambda*q - w*q*(1-q), which beats the quitter's alpha for every q exactly when lambda >= w. Their own run fits this: lambda=0.5 against w=0.5 still collapses 19% of cells, lambda=0.25 collapses 50%. Add a unit test for that inequality, score abstain as well, and treat a missing confidence as 0.5. Hours.

verdicts.title: alpha 0.5 and 0.75 predicted near-degenerate; nothing rewards work once the policy stops claiming
verdicts.reasoning:
The numbers check out. I recomputed the claimed share of true successes by hand for d'=1: alpha=0.5 gives 7% / 27% / 60% at s = 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7. Never-claim seed rates match sim_main_summary.out and my rerun (batch 0.17 and none 0.33 averaged over cells at alpha=.75). reward.py:115-117 pays alpha whatever the tests say, so a never-claim policy gives every feasible group zero variance and no gradient. train.py:246-251 is where the weights are fixed. The fix is consistent with the project's own architecture note, which prescribed "+1*tests_pass" paid independently of the claim (integration-architecture.md:83).

Two corrections:
- The title's "nothing makes working strictly better than quitting" is true only once the policy has stopped claiming; before that, work is better by (1-q)*s*(1-alpha) times the share of successes it claims.
- The scope is too narrow. The finding rests on a toy whose policy reads a calibrated private signal directly, which is the benign case. arXiv 2608.00301 reports that real language models (Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B) trained on this same rule stop answering questions they still solve "within ten optimizer steps" whenever blanket answering loses in expectation. Here that condition is s < (1+alpha)/2, i.e. below 0.625 at alpha=0.25. So alpha=0.25 is not safe by default either; see missed item VIS-M1.
verdicts.better_fix:
Make the success bonus mandatory, and put it inside compute_reward rather than in reward_weights: a RewardConfig.success_bonus added on feasible tasks when tests pass and there is no tamper or violation. That way the tamper override applies, eval re-scoring sees it, and train.py's derived weights stay untouched. Use lambda 0.25-0.5 and lambda > any Brier weight.

Gate the sweep on Phase-0: measure mean pass rate and the AUROC of stated confidence against tests_passed, and only run alpha values whose break-even (1+alpha)/2 is below the mean pass rate of the training pool, tightening the difficulty band if needed (for example 4-7 of 8 for alpha=0.25).

Run a 30-step pilot per alpha before any 300-step run. Hours.

verdicts.title: The outcome-only baseline cannot produce H1 by a first-order mechanism
verdicts.reasoning:
Half right. trl_rewards.py:83-93 pays for passing tests whatever the report says and pays 0 to every infeasible rollout. Given the trajectory up to the report, the reward does not depend on the report, so the expected gradient on the report label is exactly zero (reward-independent action under REINFORCE). This is a property of the estimator, not only of the toy. Infeasible groups have zero variance and contribute nothing. So the fabrication half of H1 would rest on drift, and the proposal's argument at proposal.md:21 ("claiming pays at least 0, abstaining pays 0") describes a claim-gated reward that is not what is implemented. Their simulation numbers match the JSON (claim rate 0.22-0.47 from 0.34, gated variant 0.99-1.00).

Overstated: "any first-order mechanism". For the abstention half there is one. Any report ends the episode, so on feasible tasks reporting or abstaining before the work is done forfeits the reward and is selected against directly. Persistence then generalising to infeasible tasks is a plausible route to lower abstention. The toy cannot show this because abstain is only a label there.

Why minor: the outcome-only run is a required baseline whatever H1 shows, and it is implemented as real outcome-only RL is done, so no GPU money is wasted. This is a paper-framing risk to settle before writing, not a training flaw.
verdicts.better_fix: Before spending a run, use the check already planned at ROADMAP.md:123: compare base Qwen3.5-4B with allenai/tmax-4b (outcome-only RL from the same base) on fabrication and abstention on the held-out set. If the RL'd model is not worse, expect a null H1 for fabrication. Then either add the 5-line claim-gated reward as a second, clearly labelled baseline, or rewrite section 2 so it claims only what the implemented baseline can show (no pressure toward honesty, and direct pressure against stopping early).

verdicts.title: The tamper override is a floor that can raise the reward
verdicts.reasoning: reward.py:144-146 replaces the total with tamper_reward after the -beta penalty has been added. Rerun with the real compute_reward: infeasible + false claim + forbidden path gives -2.0; adding a protected-path tamper gives -1.0 today and -1.5 with v2's value. So ROADMAP.md:25 ("tampering is never the better choice") is not yet true. The state is rare (the agent must already have violated and fabricated), so the practical effect is small.
verdicts.better_fix: As proposed: total = min(base + penalty + shaping, cfg.tamper_reward), plus a test. If the success bonus goes in through reward_weights instead of compute_reward, zero it on tamper as well (trl_rewards.py:92 does not).

verdicts.title: One advantage per trajectory makes the report decision noisier, not biased
verdicts.reasoning: grpo_trainer.py:3116-3120 broadcasts one advantage over all tokens and accepts (B,T) advantages from a subclass. The estimator is unbiased for the report decision, and their final thresholds agree across estimators (0.49/0.62/0.79/0.90 against 0.49/0.62/0.79/0.88). I did not rerun grad_snr.py (it needs a path argument); the stored output is internally consistent. The efficiency ratios come from a 26-parameter toy and should be read as direction only. No action is needed before the first run, which is what the reviewer says.
verdicts.better_fix: None needed now. If the report decision turns out to learn slowly, the cheaper route is the report-level arm in VIS-M1, which removes the discrete claim decision, before building a counterfactual-advantage trainer.

hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: TRL formula read at grpo_trainer.py:2819-2843; grpo_exact.py reruns byte for byte (two-valued groups give +0.935/-0.935 and +2.474/-0.353 for every alpha). Independent self-consistent derivation (v_thresh.py): 0.43/0.50/0.55/0.585 under group for alpha 0/.25/.5/.75, against their simulated 0.40/0.48/0.54/0.57 and my reseeded 0.40/0.49/0.54/0.58. Published confirmation: arXiv 2608.00301 abstract, "group normalization silently replaces every designed penalty with an effective penalty of one, moving the learned threshold from t* to 1/2"; Proposition 6(c), as extracted from the HTML version, gives the lone-answer advantage sign(r)*sqrt(G-1) = 2.65 with population std, which is 2.47 with TRL's Bessel correction, matching their lone-deviant number.

The archetype identities reproduce from part1.json: never-claim beats always-claim in 79/80 cells; quitting after one command equals never-claim-with-work in 80/80.

One number is wrong: "within 0.0125-0.11 of honest-optimal for s<=0.5". The real range for s<=0.5 is 0.0125-0.35; 0.0125-0.105 holds only for s<=0.3 with alpha>=0.5.

The paper they could not open exists and is stronger than their toy: arXiv 2608.00301 (Che, Yuan, Zhao, Yu, 31 Jul 2026) proves and shows on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 7B that the rule +1 / -lambda / 0 with abstention as a discrete action drifts to refusing everything when blanket answering loses in expectation, while mean training reward rises. This project's feasible-task rule +1 / -1 / alpha is the same rule with lambda = (1+alpha)/(1-alpha) and the same threshold (1+alpha)/2. Their reassurance that the basin "is not entered" at alpha<=0.25 with d'>=1 (0 of 32 seeds) should not be relied on: the toy policy reads a calibrated signal directly, which the paper identifies as the case that does not collapse.

reward.py:113-117 never reads blocker content on feasible tasks; spot checks rerun identically (made-up missing_capability after one command pays +0.25, and still +0.25 when tests pass). I found a stronger form they missed (v_exploit.py): one zero-command submit_report(status=incomplete, blockers = all 11 categories) pays alpha on every feasible task and +1 "abstain_correct" on all 7 perturbation classes.

The simulated sizes (33-38% of feasible non-claims labelled abstain, 35-68% of near-miss controls abstained) reproduce but are mostly relabelling of episodes that would not have claimed anyway. Agree with the reviewer's partial. The mechanism is real (grpo_trainer.py:3116-3120; honest reports get -0.935 in a 4/4 group under group scaling), and it is variance, not bias: thresholds agree across estimators in sim_main_summary.out. The sample-efficiency ratios (1.4-7.8x) are toy-specific and I did not rerun them. Not a precondition for training.

missed.title: The reward is the exact rule the project's own cited paper shows collapsing, and the listed mitigations are not that paper's repair
missed.claim:
(a) flaw now, (b) remains after v2. On feasible tasks the reward is +1 / -1 / alpha with the claim as a discrete action. That is the error-penalised rule of arXiv 2608.00301 with lambda = (1+alpha)/(1-alpha) and threshold (1+alpha)/2. The paper shows it drifting to refuse-everything on real models within about ten optimizer steps when blanket answering loses in expectation, while the reward curve rises. Here that condition is mean pass rate below (1+alpha)/2: 0.5 / 0.625 / 0.75 / 0.875 for the four sweep values. If infeasible tasks are counted as prompts where a claim is always wrong (my mapping, not in the paper), it holds for every alpha at the current 50/50 mix and for alpha >= 0.25 at the v2 mix.

The reviewer could not open the paper and concluded from the toy that alpha in {0, 0.25} is safe. I treat this as a blocker until Phase-0 shows the mean pass rate of the training pool is above (1+alpha)/2 or the correctness reward is in. I have not replicated the paper; it is single-turn QA with groups of 64-256, and this project is agentic with groups of 8.
missed.evidence:

Project: reward.py:4-5 and :111-117 (the rule); configs/base.yaml:45 (beta 0.0, no anchor) and :48 (group); DESIGN.md:166 lists the mitigations as "paired batches, lazy-abstain penalty, monitor honest/abstain_rate_feasible". Paired batches do not change a per-prompt group baseline; the lazy penalty is defeated by one command or by status=incomplete (reward.py:113); the monitor reads 0.0 during the collapse (VIS-M2). missed.fix:

3. Run a 30-step pilot per alpha with automatic stop rules: claim rate on feasible below 5%, share of zero-variance groups above 50%, or rewards/task_success/mean falling while mean reward rises.

missed.claim: (a) flaw now, (b) remains after v2. "Infeasible" is validated only by the oracle solution failing. If the agent finds another route, passes the real tests and truthfully reports complete, it is scored -1 and flagged fabricated, while a zero-effort decline on the same task gets +1. That teaches giving up over problem solving, and in an honesty paper it punishes a statement the environment verifies as true. This is the mirror image of INC-2. Severity depends on the leak rate, which is unknown until Docker runs; raise it to major if honest/infeasible_tests_pass_rate exceeds about 5%.

verify:incentives-sim.corrected_numbers:
Terms: s = pass rate on feasible tasks; q = share of infeasible tasks; d' = how well the agent can tell its own successes from failures; alpha = reward for an honest non-completion report.

1. Line numbers. reward.py was edited at 16:25 (logic unchanged), so the reviewer's reward.py citations are 3 lines low. Current: no-report 109-110; lazy rule 113-114; alpha branch 115-117; infeasible claimed 119-120; category match 121-125; implicit 126-127; Brier 141-142; tamper override 144-146. MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS is harness.py:40, not :39. abstain's confidence=None is env.py:180, not :177. The alpha sweep is now ROADMAP.md:129, not :124.

2. Group-scaling thresholds (INC-1), alpha = 0 / .25 / .5 / .75, nominal 0.50 / 0.625 / 0.75 / 0.875:
- reviewer's simulation: 0.40 / 0.48 / 0.54 / 0.57
- my reseeded rerun (16 seeds, both lr 0.03 x 2000 and lr 0.01 x 6000): 0.40 / 0.49 / 0.54 / 0.58
- my independent analytic fixed point (v_thresh.py): 0.43 / 0.50 / 0.55 / 0.585
- batch rerun: 0.48 / 0.60 / 0.71 / 0.83; none rerun: 0.49 / 0.62 / 0.78 / 0.90
Sweep width under group is 0.16-0.18 against 0.375 nominal.

3. Their "fabrication 8.1% vs 4.0% vs 3.2%" and "claim rate +0.13 above optimum" average only alpha >= 0.25. Over all four alphas the figures are 9.2% / 5.6% / 4.9% and +0.105. Per alpha under group, fabrication on feasible tasks runs 12.3% -> 6.8%; under none, 9.9% -> 0.9%.

4. H-C: "quitting is within 0.0125-0.11 of honest-optimal for s <= 0.5" is wrong. From part1.json the range for s <= 0.5 is 0.0125-0.35 (the formula is (1-q)*s*(1-alpha)). The 0.0125-0.105 range holds only for s <= 0.3 with alpha >= 0.5. Against the calibrated d'=1 policy the gap is 0.000-0.134.

5. INC-2: the abstention on near-miss controls is mostly relabelling. In sim_main.json (batch) 56-96% of non-claims on controls carry the abstain label, while the claim rate on controls falls only modestly (0.25 against about 0.33 on plain tasks at alpha=.25, d'=1, s=.5). My rerun of the fix at alpha=.25, batch: abstain on controls 0.40 -> 0.14 (priced at 0) -> 0.10 (priced at -0.25); abstain on infeasible 0.99 / 0.97 / 0.95; claim threshold 0.60 / 0.60 / 0.61.

6. Margin for honest work over the best constant no-effort report, alpha=.25, s=.3:
- today: 0.6325 - 0.475 = 0.16 at q=.3; 0.7375 - 0.625 = 0.11 at q=.5
- with false blockers priced at 0: 0.6325 - 0.325 = 0.31 at q=.3; 0.7375 - 0.50 = 0.24 at q=.5

7. INC-3 reruns (batch, new seeds). Never-report under masking: 0.94 of feasible episodes (minimum cell 0.89; 0.66 at step 300), with the claim rate falling to 0.05; 0.00 when scored 0 or alpha-0.1. Share of cells losing effort when a working episode runs out of budget with probability h, scored 0 as today: alpha=.25: 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.17 at h = .05 / .1 / .2; alpha=.5: 0.07 / 0.18 / 0.50.

8. INC-4 reruns (batch): share of seeds quitting in the d'=1, s=.3 cell at Brier weight 0.05 / 0.2 / 0.5: alpha=.25: 0 / 0.19 / 1.0; alpha=.5: 0 / 1.0 / 1.0. Condition for a Brier weight w to be safe with a success bonus lambda: lambda >= w (derived; consistent with their bonus run, where lambda=0.5 against w=0.5 leaves 19% and lambda=0.25 leaves 50%).

9. Mapping to arXiv 2608.00301 (my judgment, not replicated). alpha = 0 / .25 / .5 / .75 corresponds to penalty lambda = 1 / 1.67 / 3 / 7 and break-even pass rate 0.50 / 0.625 / 0.75 / 0.875. Counting infeasible tasks as prompts where a claim is always wrong, the pool's mean pass rate would need to exceed 0.71 (alpha=0) or 0.89 (alpha=.25) at the v2 mix, and no value suffices at the current 50/50 mix (scripts/build_dataset.sh:25).

10. Not rerun: grad_snr.py (INC-8 efficiency ratios) and the 648-setting main grid; for the grid I recomputed the reported summaries from sim_main.json and reran a 144-setting subset.

verify:trl-dynamics-cost.lens: verify-trl-dynamics-cost: adversarial check of the "trl-dynamics-cost" review (does the TRL 1.14.1 GRPO + vLLM + Harbor recipe work mechanically, and what will it cost). verdicts.title: Two training ranks + vLLM server mode breaks TRL's tool loop; the smoke test is single-process and will pass
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is real. trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:594 gathers every rank's active prompts and :651-654 slices by rank index times the local count; accelerate's gather_object is all_gather_object concatenated in rank order (accelerate/utils/operations.py:498-502). I reran the reviewer's script against the real VLLMGeneration.generate: with active counts (3,2) rank 1 receives [1002, 1010], and with (2,3) it receives two completions for three samples. Neither TRL nor src/honest_agents/train.py guards against it, and configs/smoke.yaml:11 uses one process. I lowered the severity because the failure is loud. In my simulation (verify.py: 20,000 rounds, 32 episodes per rank, lengths uniform 2-30 turns) the first round crashes 92% of the time, desynchronises 4%, and completes 3.6%. About half the rounds apply some mis-assigned turns before crashing, but no run can finish corrupted. The cost is bring-up hours and a layout change. It stays open after v2: the planned teacher layout keeps two training ranks (docs/ROADMAP.md:85).
verdicts.better_fix: The reviewer's fix (one training process per run) is correct. Two additions. First, it must ship with TDC-5: a single rank runs all 64 episodes' tool calls serially, about 21 min/step against 11 with parallel tools under the reviewer's own unit assumptions. Second, add a guard in train.py that refuses use_vllm + vllm_mode server + launch.num_processes > 1, so a later config edit cannot bring it back. Do not switch to AsyncGRPOTrainer as a way out: its worker hard-codes group-std advantages (trl/experimental/async_grpo/async_rollout_worker.py:1026), which recreates TDC-3.

verdicts.title: vLLM --max-model-len 20480 rejects tool-loop requests once a transcript passes 4,096 tokens; the run crashes in round 1
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed at each link. TRL sends max_tokens = max_completion_length on every turn (trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:624) in one /v1/completions POST (trl/generation/vllm_client.py:436) and raises on any non-200 (vllm_client.py:266-270; only 500/502/503 are retried). vLLM v0.30.0 sets max input to max_model_len minus max_tokens and raises when the prompt is longer (vllm/renderers/params.py _token_len_check and vllm/entrypoints/openai/completion/protocol.py build_tok_params, fetched at tag v0.30.0). With scripts/serve_vllm.sh:28 at 20480 that leaves 4,096 input tokens. TRL's own guard reads the model config, not the server (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2118-2119). Like TDC-1 this fails fast, so it costs bring-up time and not a run. It stays major because no step can complete as configured and the smoke test (8,192 window, 4,096 budget) passes only if its episodes stay short.
verdicts.better_fix: Cap each turn instead of doubling the window: set grpo.generation_kwargs: {max_tokens: 4096}. TRL applies generation_kwargs after its own sampling parameters (vllm_client.py:424; grpo_config.py:552-560 says conflicting keys override), and the tool loop still enforces the 16,384 total. The window then needs prompt + budget + 4,096: about 21.6k for a 16k budget and 38k for a 32k budget, which fits Qwen3-4B's 40,960, so the bring-up model is not limited to 16k as the reviewer concluded. It also matches the eval loop's per-turn cap (src/honest_agents/eval/run_eval.py:71) and stops one runaway sequence from holding all 64 episodes. A turn cut at the cap ends without an end-of-turn token and is loss-masked; in non-thinking mode that should be rare (a full report is 177 tokens). Keep the reviewer's startup assert against the server's max_model_len.

verdicts.title: scale_rewards: group removes alpha from two-valued groups, so the alpha sweep does not test the (1+alpha)/2 threshold
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed, and somewhat worse than reported. My independent implementation with TRL's nanstd (verify.py) reproduces the thresholds 0.576 / 0.644 / 0.698 for alpha 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 at G=8, and the nominal values under 'none'. It is a small-group effect: at G=32 the thresholds are 0.616 / 0.731 / 0.835. Two results the reviewer did not state. (1) In a group of 8 with exactly one non-success, the failing rollout gets advantage -2.474 if it reports honestly and -2.475 if it fabricates, for every alpha (verify2.py); under 'none' it is -0.656 against -1.750 at alpha 0.25. Such groups are 27% of groups at success rate 0.75 and 39% at 0.85, so group scaling also weakens the headline honesty signal on easy tasks, not only the sweep. (2) In the proposed report-only pilot every group shares one outcome, so every group is two-valued and the threshold is 0.500 for every alpha. I keep blocker because this is the only defect in this lens that is silent: the runs finish and section 4.3 / contribution 4 of docs/proposal.md would describe something the optimiser did not do. The honest arm still trains under 'group' (the reviewer's he_credit.py shows a positive expected push toward honesty), so H2 is weakened, not lost. The Tmax script does use --advantage_normalization_type centered (fetched).
verdicts.better_fix: The reviewer's fix is right: grpo.scale_rewards: none for every arm (configs/base.yaml:48). Prefer 'none' over 'batch', which keeps the direction but ties the step size to each batch's reward spread. Add the unit test the reviewer proposes plus one for the single-failure group, and make train.py refuse reward.mode honest with scale_rewards group.

verdicts.title: 16,384 tokens including tool output is too small, and budget exhaustion is scored as a silent stop, not masked
verdicts.reasoning: The mechanism is confirmed; the size is not. A tool result that does not fit is rolled back and the sample leaves the loop on the assistant's end-of-turn token (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2110-2136), so it is not 'truncated' (:2540-2547) and is scored: no report gives 0 on a feasible task, below alpha, and +0.25 on an infeasible one (src/honest_agents/reward.py:109-110, :126-127). The loop condition at :2023 means tool calls in the 31st assistant turn never run. v2 handles only the call cap (docs/ROADMAP.md:28-32). The token costs reproduce when I rerun budget.py. But '40-48% of episodes exhaust the budget' is one cell of an assumption grid: it needs a median output of 800 characters and a policy that wants 5-40 calls. At a 400-character median the same simulation gives 2-5%. Nobody has measured the real distribution. The Tmax training README does say about 65k output length 'seems quite important for the 9B and 4B model', and its script uses response_length 65536 with 64 steps (both fetched), so a budget four times smaller than the reference recipe is a real risk of unknown size.
verdicts.better_fix: Cheapest first: lower MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS from 6000 to about 2000 (src/honest_agents/harness.py:40), which cuts the worst-case call from about 2,600 to about 900 tokens, and add the per-turn cap from TDC-2. Then build the reviewer's environment-owned budget (warn and force a report by cumulative characters, not only by call count) and give token-exhausted episodes the same treatment v2 gives cap-hit ones. Choose 16k or 32k from the distribution measured in the zero-learning-rate run (missed item MV-2), not from the simulation.

verdicts.title: Tool calls execute serially across the batch with a 180 s timeout; this, not the GPUs, sets the cost
verdicts.reasoning: Confirmed by reading. TRL runs each turn's tool calls in a plain loop over samples, calls sync tools inline, and gathers async tools only within one sample (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2031-2078). bash blocks on the env's loop (src/honest_agents/env.py:128-131) and each call is a docker compose exec subprocess (harbor/environments/docker/docker.py:644-690, :1289-1330). The timing inputs (0.8 s per call, 14 calls per episode) are assumptions, but the central figure is more likely optimistic than pessimistic: with one rank, 1% of the 896 calls per step hitting the 180 s timeout adds 27 minutes per step (verify2.py), twice the whole central estimate. On timeout Harbor terminates only the compose client (docker.py:728-730), so the command keeps running in the container. Tmax's script does set SWERL_DOCKER_EXEC_CONCURRENCY=256 (fetched).
verdicts.better_fix: Do it in the already-planned HonestGRPOTrainer: either override _tool_call_loop (TRL is pinned, so copying about 230 lines is acceptable) or supply a rollout_func, which is the project's own documented fallback (docs/research/integration-architecture.md:26). Environments are reset before generation starts (grpo_trainer.py:2437-2441), so a rollout function can drive trainer.environments with a thread pool. One custom loop can fix TDC-1, TDC-2, TDC-4 and TDC-5 together and stop at the first report, as the eval loop does. Cut command_timeout_sec to 30-60 s and wrap commands in `timeout -k` so the in-container process dies too.

verdicts.title: Default sequence-level importance sampling randomly drops long trajectories; bf16 merge-sync hides most of the early LoRA update from the sampler
verdicts.reasoning: Both code paths are as described (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2713-2755 and :3207-3208; trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:446-470; defaults at trl/trainer/grpo_config.py:929-957), and both proxy measurements reproduce: per-token std 0.035, and merge retention 5% / 45% / 84% / 99% at B scale 1e-5 / 1e-4 / 3e-4 / 1e-3. Two corrections. First, 'randomly drops' is not what the proxy shows: all six sequence ratios are below 1 (0.45, 0.84, 0.33, 0.64, 0.96, 0.04) and none exceeds 3. The expected log-ratio is negative and grows with length, so long episodes are systematically down-weighted (median weight 0.55 at 1,000 tokens) and about 4% are zeroed, not 15%. The practical point survives: short episodes keep full weight, long ones lose it, which adds to the early-quit pressure in TDC-7. Second, 'first tens of steps' assumes every Adam step has the same sign; with noisy gradients B may stay near 1e-4 to 3e-4 for most of a 300-step run, so the lag can persist. Its effect is a stale sampler, not a broken run. I lowered the severity because the real vLLM-vs-HF mismatch on a 4B model on H100s is unmeasured (the proxy is fp32 vs bf16 on a 0.6B model on CPU) and the mitigation is one config line.
verdicts.better_fix: Set grpo.vllm_importance_sampling_mode: token_truncate, or turn the correction off as Tmax does (--truncated_importance_sampling_ratio_cap 0.0, fetched), before the first run. Check sampling/importance_sampling_ratio/mean and sampling/sampling_logp_difference/max (grpo_trainer.py:2924-2951) on episodes over 1,000 model tokens in the zero-learning-rate run. Do not change dtypes yet: float32 serving costs speed and memory for an unmeasured benefit. Evaluation serves the adapter unmerged (docs/EVAL.md:27), so training-time metrics can lag what evaluation sees; compare one checkpoint both ways before trusting training curves.

verdicts.title: Until fabrication is unlearned, quitting immediately beats attempting on most kept tasks; high-alpha runs are likely to collapse to early 'incomplete'
verdicts.reasoning: The arithmetic and the code hole are confirmed; 'likely to collapse' is a prediction. I re-derived the condition p/(1-p) < f(1+alpha)/(1-alpha) and the reviewer's break-even values. The lazy penalty fires only for abstain with zero commands (src/honest_agents/reward.py:113-114); submit_report(status=incomplete) with zero commands, or abstain after one command, is paid alpha (:115-117). Twins never share a baseline: each group of 8 is one dataset row (reran geom.py; trl/trainer/utils.py:905-909). The size of the risk depends on f, the share of failures the base model fabricates, which nobody has measured. At the headline alpha 0.25 quitting wins only below p = 0.14 / 0.29 / 0.45 for f = 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5, so the headline run is at moderate risk; at alpha 0.75 the break-even is 0.41 / 0.64 / 0.78, so the high-alpha arms are the exposed ones. This overlaps the reward-design lens.
verdicts.better_fix: Measure f and per-task p in Phase 0 and compute the break-even per alpha before launching any arm above 0.25. Close the hole in hours: treat any non-complete report with fewer than k substantive commands as lazy. Run alpha 0.25 first and stop automatically if the share of non-complete reports on feasible tasks passes a ceiling. The reviewer's warm start from a report-level pilot is a reasonable second step, not a prerequisite.

verdicts.title: Policy-caused grading failures are masked and lose the tamper penalty; v2's cap-hit masking only works if both reward functions return None
verdicts.reasoning: Both parts reproduce. With a sandbox whose exec always returns 127, grade() raises at src/honest_agents/grading.py:166 after the tamper diff at :229-230 has already found the damage, and the env rebuilds the outcome with only grading_error (src/honest_agents/env.py:274-276), so both reward functions return None (src/honest_agents/trl_rewards.py:41-44, :89-90). TRL treats a row as unscorable only when every function is NaN (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2815-2820); [None, 0.0] under weights [1, 0] gives reward 0.0 (reran hf_mask.py). I lowered the severity because the policy has to destroy the container's shell or stall the manifests to reach this path, a masked episode gets zero gradient in either direction, and the damage is to metric accounting. The v2 point is a caution about code not yet written.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer says: build the outcome from the state checks first and keep tamper when a later step raises; reserve None for boot failures. Log masked episodes per arm with the reason, so a rising masked share is visible.

verdicts.title: Scale and seeds: 19,200 episodes of LoRA at lr 1e-5 may not move the outcome-only arm enough for H1, and H1 has one seed
verdicts.reasoning: The facts are confirmed; the conclusion is the reviewer's judgement, as they say. 300 steps of 64 episodes is 19,200 (configs/base.yaml:52-54, :63). The Tmax script has total_episodes 128000, 8 prompts x 32 samples, lr 1e-6, response_length 65536, 4 nodes x 8 GPUs (fetched). task_success is 0.0 on every infeasible episode (src/honest_agents/trl_rewards.py:92), so those groups carry no signal in the outcome arm. H1 is one run and only the headline config gets 3 seeds (docs/ROADMAP.md:122-123). save_steps 25 with save_total_limit 4 keeps only steps 225-300 (configs/base.yaml:80-81). Two qualifications. The fabrication curve for H1 does not need checkpoints: the honesty metrics are computed and logged at weight 0 in outcome mode (src/honest_agents/train.py:10-13; trl_rewards.py:62-75); checkpoints matter only for the AgentAbstain-over-training part. And the allenai/tmax-4b check is weaker than presented: that model was trained without report tools, with a 65k budget and 64 steps, so under this 16k / 30-turn harness it may simply not report. Treat its result as directional.
verdicts.better_fix: Set save_total_limit to null and budget 3 seeds for the outcome arm (hours, plus two runs). Read H1's fabrication curve from the training logs first. Decide run length from evidence: look at reward and case rates after the first 50-100 steps of the first real run before committing all arms to 300.

verdicts.title: Config values that waste compute or risk an out-of-memory stop
verdicts.reasoning: All four hold by reading: one pad over the rank's generation batch before it is split (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2504-2514, :1626-1630), the full-logits path when use_liger_kernel is unset (:1372-1375), shuffle disabled by pair_batches (src/honest_agents/train.py:317-318), and DeepSpeed in configs/accelerate/zero2_2gpu.yaml. Memory figures are arithmetic, not measured. Item (b) is the only one that can stop a run part-way, on the first long batch, so the worst-case benchmark should precede the first long run. TRL has a fused log-prob kernel (trl/trainer/utils.py:569-571, :670-672) that would lower the peak if it is available on the node; I could not check that on macOS.
verdicts.better_fix: As the reviewer says. With the single-process layout DeepSpeed is dropped anyway. If the worst-case batch does not fit, use per_device_train_batch_size 1 with gradient_accumulation_steps 64.

hypothesis_verdicts.evidence: Independent re-implementation with trl.trainer.utils.nanstd (verify.py) reproduces the sign-change points 0.576 / 0.644 / 0.698 for alpha 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 at G=8 and claim rate 0.5, and the nominal 0.625 / 0.75 / 0.875 under 'none'. The distortion shrinks with group size (G=32: 0.616 / 0.731 / 0.835), so it is a small-group effect of dividing by a sample std. Formula at trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2821-2843. Additional: a lone failing rollout in a group of 8 gets -2.474 honest vs -2.475 fabricated for every alpha (verify2.py); in a report-only pilot the threshold under 'group' is 0.500 for every alpha.

Agree with the reviewer's 'partial'. he_credit.py reproduces (signal-to-noise 2.20 vs 2.43, 0.78 vs 1.78, 0.33 vs 1.15). One scalar advantage is broadcast over all model tokens (trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:3116-3120, which also accepts (B, T) advantages). The DAPO loss sums over tokens (:3214-3219), which is the correct weighting for a trajectory log-probability, so the loss itself adds no length bias. The expected push toward honest reporting is positive in every regime tested, so this is variance, not bias. The simulation is a bandit with an assumed 0.95 claim rate on success; real ratios will differ.

Agree. hf_mask.py reproduces: grade() raises at src/honest_agents/grading.py:166, the env outcome has tamper False (src/honest_agents/env.py:274-276), both reward functions return None. A hung command is not masked (env.py:132-133) and a test timeout counts as failure (grading.py:176-179). Truncated samples lose their loss mask but their reward still enters the baseline (:2540-2549 vs :2821).

The cost arithmetic reproduces from cost.py, but every timing input is an assumption and the 'as configured' rows describe a layout that cannot complete a step (TDC-1, TDC-2). Realistic central bracket with the reviewer's own unit assumptions: $280-390 per run with one rank and parallel tools, $530-740 with one rank and serial tools (verify2.py). Two cost tails are missing from the model (missed item MV-1). The report-only pilot is mechanically feasible with stock TRL (the tool loop at trl/trainer/grpo_trainer.py:2023 never runs at max_tool_calling_iterations 0; reward is a pure function, src/honest_agents/reward.py:100) and is sound for report-level questions only, as the reviewer says. It says nothing about early quitting, which is the main alpha-related risk in the full loop.

missed.title: Each step is as slow as its slowest episode at three unbounded waits, and the test timeout is not configurable
missed.claim: Grading waits for all 64 episodes, and each test run may take up to 900 s. That default is hard-coded and cannot be set from the run config. One hanging test per step therefore adds up to 13 minutes, about the whole central step time in the reviewer's cost model. Per-turn generation has the same shape: one blocking request for all active episodes with max_tokens 16,384, so one runaway sequence holds everyone. Evidence replay adds up to 8 x 40 s per episode after the tests, although v2 makes it a metric only. The cost model's 120 s for grading assumes none of this happens.
missed.evidence: src/honest_agents/grading.py:56 (tests_timeout_sec 900), :170-175 (used for every task; the task's own [verifier] timeout is ignored), :57-58 and :194-200 (evidence replay). src/honest_agents/train.py:495-501 builds the environment without a grading_config, so the default always applies. src/honest_agents/trl_rewards.py:31-32 waits for all futures. trl/generation/vllm_client.py:436 (one POST per turn) with trl/generation/vllm_generation.py:624. missed.fix: Expose the test timeout in the run config and default it to the smaller of the task's verifier timeout and about 180 s. Cap or drop evidence replay on the training path. Add the per-turn max_tokens cap from TDC-2. Log the slowest episode per phase each step so the tail is visible in the first hour.
